newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Firmer Australian bonds quiet, seen well supported.
newsitem.headline: Firmer Australian bonds quiet, seen well supported.

text.p: *Australian bonds off to firmer, but slow start, in a week expected to be dominated by technical trading and the U.S.
*Local bonds expected to be well-supported by expectations of favourable inflation and wages data next week.

Australian bonds were firmer in early trade after the U.S. market strengthened on Friday, and traders said they should remain well-supported ahead of the release of second quarter inflation and wage data next week. U.S. 30-year Treasury yields fell to their lowest levels so far this year after a tame June producer price index helped confirm that U.S. inflation pressures remained contained.

"We've got nothing out really this week, and there's some important data out in the U.S. over the course of the week, so I think we'll just have technical trading type of week, following the U.S. around," one trader said.
That meant the week's open was quiet, with the underlying positive tone supported by expectations a local rate cut would follow favourable inflation and wages data next week.

Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the key underlying inflation rate, the measure targetted by the Reserve Bank, to fall to 1.7 percent, below the two to three target zone and the lowest level recorded since the series began in the early 1970s.

There are no major data due this week which was helping to keep things quiet. Partial price indicators, including May manufacturing output prices on Monday, were expected to point to a picture of subdued inflation pressures.

Spreads generally narrower at the open, reversing some of Friday's widening, as local market remains well-supported by rate cut hopes. Over week, spreads expected to hold, with market expected to follow any U.S. rally.
